words: Brain injury, chemicals, illness, and anesthesia disrupt consciousness, while scans map thoughts and emotions to neuronal firing, supporting natural brain dependence over an immaterial immortal soul.
critique: Strongest feature: The move links brain injury, chemicals, illness, and anesthesia causing unconsciousness with precise scans associating thoughts and emotions with neuronal firing, then cites laboratory testing of brain-produced consciousness models. Principal limitation: Dependence and correlation favor natural explanation, but neither proves every conscious feature is brain-produced nor excludes an immaterial soul operating through physical conditions, leaving evidence warrant and calibration weaker. Live burden: It must show why physical modulation and testable models establish production rather than dependence alone and thereby preclude consciousness continuing after death. Locked score: The exact score of 80 fits because responsiveness is stronger in directly challenging postmortem consciousness, whereas evidence warrant and calibration are weaker since models and scan associations fall short of decisive exclusion.
